title: First human epigenetic reprogramming trial advances as FDA opens the door to rejuvenation medicine
description: Life Biosciences has dosed its first Phase 1 patients with ER-100, an OSK partial-reprogramming gene therapy for optic neuropathies, the first time epigenetic reprogramming has been given to humans. Paired with the FDA's new Plausible Mechanism Pathway, it signals regulators warming to aging-reversal science.

title: Senescence mapping goes granular: how aged cells spread dysfunction across brain and fat tissue
description: New work details how five senescent brain-cell types signal neighbors into senescence, and how senescent fat cells release ANGPTL8 to drive inflammation and cardiometabolic risk. Together they sharpen senescence as a systemic, targetable driver of aging.

title: AI 'virtual cell' models arrive as computation reshapes longevity R&D
description: GenBio, co-founded by Nobel laureate David Baker, launched a 'world model' of a cell that simulates cellular behavior, while a new transcriptomic clock ('Pasta') predicts the age-related effects of compounds and gene expression. Simulation-first discovery is becoming a core longevity toolset.

title: Longevity biotech funding surges, with epigenetic reprogramming leading the capital race
description: Longevity biotech raised roughly $3.74B across 49 financings in Q1 2026, up 56% year over year, with reprogramming players like NewLimit and Life Biosciences capturing the largest rounds. Capital is concentrating in a handful of platform bets.

title: Longevity's safety and standards reckoning intensifies after infusion death and clinic self-regulation push
description: In the wake of a death after a NAD+ 'longevity infusion,' the field is moving to self-regulate: Longevity Clinics World and the Healthy Longevity Medicine Society signed an MOU on shared terminology, evidence standards, and accreditation, underscoring the gap between consumer marketing and clinical evidence.

title: A Tougher Extracellular Matrix Strengthens Tendons in Rats
description: Researchers found that an upstream promoter of two extracellular matrix proteins improved healing and strength in rat tendons, pointing to a route for addressing age-related decline in connective tissue repair.

title: In ALS, Microglia Eat Living Neurons, Mistaking Them for Dead
description: A new study suggests that in ALS, and possibly other neurodegenerative diseases, the brain's immune cells devour stressed but still-living neurons, offering a potential intervention point for age-related neurodegeneration.

title: How Old Fat Cells Trigger Inflammation and Raise Risks
description: Using cohort studies and a mouse model, researchers found that ANGPTL8, a circulating factor produced by senescent fat cells, is linked to inflammation and elevated metabolic disease risk with age.

title: GenBio Launches a 'Virtual Cell' AI Model
description: AI startup GenBio, which lists Nobel laureate David Baker among its co-founders, announced a 'world model' of a cell capable of simulating cellular behavior, a tool aimed at accelerating aging and disease research.

title: How Senescence Spreads Between Brain Cells
description: Researchers detailed how each of five senescent brain-cell types expresses and receives factors that push neighboring cells toward senescence, mapping a mechanism behind spreading brain aging.

title: Fight Aging! Newsletter: Weekly Longevity Research Digest, August 17th 2026
description: Fight Aging!'s weekly roundup of longevity research and commentary, covering mechanisms of aging, senescence, and emerging rejuvenation strategies aimed at bringing aging under medical control.

title: A Million-Person Study Finds a Protective Metabolic Gene
description: A large human genetics study identified rare FNIP1 mutations associated with favorable metabolism and much lower cardiometabolic disease risk, validated in follow-up experiments on human cells.

title: A Drug Combination Fights Both Senescence and Cancer
description: Writing in Aging, the Conboy lab described a combination treatment that kills both senescent and cancer cells and extended lifespan in old mice, linking senotherapy with anti-cancer effects.

title: Forever Healthy Launches the Evipedia Browser Extension
description: The Forever Healthy Foundation released Evipedia, a browser extension that surfaces evidence summaries for longevity interventions and supplements to help consumers assess claims more quickly.

title: The Thymus Hormone Thymulin Reduces Inflammaging in Mice
description: A study identified the thymus hormone thymulin as an age-dependent suppressor of inflammation; treating cancer-bearing mice with it reduced inflammatory signaling, pointing to a lever on immune aging.

title: Why Affecting Aging in Complex Organisms Is So Hard
description: A new theoretical framework proposes why more complex animals are harder to move with aging interventions, with implications for translating simple-organism results to mammals and humans.

title: A New Target Against High Blood Pressure
description: Researchers uncovered why the protein AGGF1 significantly affects blood pressure, reporting in Aging Cell a potential target for age-related hypertension and vascular dysfunction.

title: A New Transcriptomic Clock for Intervention Analysis
description: A team developed 'Pasta,' a transcriptomic aging clock that predicts the age-related effects of various compounds and gene-expression changes, offering a tool for screening interventions.

title: Life Biosciences Doses First Patient in Phase 1 Trial of ER-100 for Optic Neuropathies
description: Life Biosciences dosed the first participant in its Phase 1 trial of ER-100, an OSK partial epigenetic reprogramming therapy for open-angle glaucoma and NAION, the first administration of cellular reprogramming to a human. Up to 18 participants are planned.

title: FDA Greenlights Life Biosciences' Gene Therapy Study to Rewind the Age of Cells
description: The FDA cleared Life Biosciences' IND for ER-100, an epigenetic partial-reprogramming therapy for the human eye, an early regulatory milestone for aging-reversal approaches now progressing into human testing.

title: Two-Year Randomized Trial Tests Metformin to Reduce Frailty in Older Adults
description: A double-blind, placebo-controlled trial randomized older adults with glucose intolerance to 24 months of metformin or placebo to assess effects on frailty, part of ongoing efforts to test repurposed drugs as geroprotectors.

title: Rapamycin in Alzheimer's and Aging: the ERAP Phase IIa Imaging Study
description: The ERAP Phase IIa protocol evaluates whether six months of rapamycin changes cerebral glucose uptake in early-stage Alzheimer's, testing the mTOR inhibitor as a geroprotector in humans after supportive preclinical data.

title: Advanced Anti-Aging Therapies: What Human Data Show for Senolytics, NAD+ and Rapamycin in 2026
description: A 2026 review assesses the current clinical evidence for leading geroprotector candidates, noting senolytics (D+Q, fisetin) are generally well tolerated and NAD+ precursors show modest physical-performance gains, while no molecule yet meets the bar for an approved anti-aging drug.

title: NewLimit Raises $435M Ahead of Its First Clinical Trial
description: Epigenetic-reprogramming startup NewLimit raised $435M to advance toward its first human trial, one of the year's largest longevity rounds and a sign of investor appetite for reprogramming platforms.

title: Longevity Biotech Investment 2026: Set for a Breakout Year
description: An analysis of 2026 longevity financing finds capital accelerating and increasingly concentrated in a few platform companies, with epigenetic reprogramming the clearest momentum category heading into the second half.

title: Viome Acquires Circulate Health to Fuse Diagnostics With Plasma Exchange
description: Viome's acquisition of Circulate Health folds therapeutic plasma exchange into a diagnostics, nutrition and coaching platform spanning 200+ partner clinics, building a 'measure, act, remeasure' longevity model.

title: The Longevity Industry Is Building Its Own Rules
description: A roundup on how the longevity field is assembling clinical standards, biological models and infrastructure, including a Longevity Clinics World and Healthy Longevity Medicine Society MOU on evidence-based standards and accreditation governance.

title: Wei-Wu He: People Should Become the CEOs of Their Own Health
description: An interview with Human Longevity Inc.'s Wei-Wu He on data-driven, genomics-based personal health management and the evolving business of preventive longevity medicine.

title: Why Democratizing Rejuvenation Is an Economic Imperative
description: A Lifespan Research Institute whitepaper argues that treating the biology of aging, rather than only its late-stage diseases, is essential to contain unsustainable healthcare costs at population scale.

title: Small Concurrent Gains in Sleep, Activity and Nutrition Extend Lifespan and Healthspan
description: A UK Biobank cohort study of tens of thousands of participants found that modest simultaneous improvements across sleep, physical activity and diet were associated with meaningful gains in both lifespan and healthspan.

title: Exercise Interventions Improve Subjective Sleep Quality in Older Adults
description: A systematic review and meta-analysis using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index found that structured exercise interventions improved sleep quality in older adults, reinforcing exercise as a high-ROI healthspan protocol.

title: Valine Restriction Increases Male Mouse Lifespan by 23%
description: Restricting the amino acid valine extended both median and maximum lifespan in male mice and improved healthspan in both sexes, adding to evidence for targeted dietary restriction as an aging intervention.
